official instructions
Install a compatible FoxHole OpenWrt Client using the official instructions.
Check compatibility
Connect to the Wi-Fi network of your OpenWrt router. For first pairing, turn off any active VPN on your phone. If Android asks for local-network access, grant permission.
Install a compatible FoxHole OpenWrt Client using the official instructions.
Install a compatible FoxHole OpenWrt Client using the official instructions, or use the in-app setup wizard (beta) to install the package on a supported router.
After installing the package manually, open LuCI → Services → FoxHole and set the owner PIN if it has not been configured. There is no preset PIN.
Open Router in the app. Find the router or enter its private local address, tap Connect and enter the PIN.

FoxHole does not install or update OpenWrt firmware. You need your own VPN profile or provider subscription. Manage the router VPN in the web panel or a FoxHole app. Open FoxHole OpenWRT at the router address; use the web panel button to switch between FoxHole and LuCI.
Profiles, exported configurations and subscription URLs may contain access secrets. Share them only with people and routers you trust. Transfer is not continuous two-way profile synchronization.

In the router settings, enable “Home VPN server” and confirm the action. Router → phone: open VPN clients, create a client profile and tap IMPORT TO PHONE. The inbound VPN profile connects the phone to the home router, where the current routing rules apply. This requires a configured inbound Hysteria2 server, a reachable public IPv4 address and a UDP port. A provider’s Static IP service is one suitable option.
Connecting to the router over VPN requires a reachable public IPv4 address and an open UDP port supported by the current configuration. Local and foreign traffic routes are configured in Settings.

Smart disconnects only the active home VPN profile imported from this paired router when you join the confirmed home Wi-Fi network with verified VPN routing. On cellular, it reconnects the same unchanged profile. “Home VPN server” and “Manage over mobile networks” must be enabled. Other profiles, Wi-Fi networks, and manual actions are not overridden. Smart is off by default and requires the monitoring notification. Reconnection starts within 90 seconds after home Wi-Fi is lost, not after VPN disconnects. Manual control or profile changes cancel the transition.
If the router certificate changes, check the device and the cause first. Do not ignore an identity mismatch or bypass certificate verification.

WireGuard domain rules require Android 11/API 30 or later. Application blocking in Proxy requires Android 10/API 29. IP rules and ordinary application routing keep their own platform and protocol limits.
Use the top-right switch to choose website routing settings.

WireGuard with website rules or blocked applications checks the authenticated profile DNS server. Exit IP and location are unavailable in that mode and Geo refresh is refused. Connected confirms that check, not reachability of every website.

Profiles and settings are encrypted on the device with Android Keystore. No advertising or analytics SDK is included; GPS is not needed. Signed TLS tables come from FoxHole DB; subscriptions use your saved provider URLs.
In regular validation modes, checks connectivity through the selected VPN network. The service receives the request and source IP.

Provides approximate IP location. VPN checks use the selected VPN; location refresh without VPN, including widgets, uses the current internet connection. The service receives the request and source IP.
AmneziaWG is experimental. Protocol and route availability depend on the imported profile and the installed native build.
Subscriptions use your saved provider URL. When background refresh is enabled, the default interval is 12 hours; supported profiles can refresh automatically.

FoxHole DB supplies signed data, not executable code. TLS fingerprint tables are checked every 24 hours by default when enabled; installing prepared data needs your action. Other datasets follow their feature settings.
The GitHub build checks for app updates daily. Downloading and installation require your action and Android confirmation. F-Droid updates the F-Droid build.
Tap “+” and choose an available option to import a configuration or an HTTPS provider subscription.
Choose a supported configuration file.
Scan a profile QR code with the camera.
Select the saved profile and, when applicable, the server/protocol option.
Tap Start and approve Android’s system VPN request.
Check the connection state. Stop cancels connecting and disconnects VPN.
Enter a supported connection link manually in the add-profile field.

Phone to router: long-press a saved profile and tap “Send config to router.” A v2rayTun subscription is not transferred in full; only the selected compatible node is sent. You can also tap “+” in the “Manage” header of router management. The app searches all saved profiles and subscriptions for compatible configurations. Select one or more and tap “Transfer.” Only selected nodes are transferred; then choose the profile on the router and start the VPN separately.
The “Whole device” scenario routes all traffic through VPN and ignores app rules.
The Proxy scenario applies VPN / Direct rules.
With Whole device enabled, all traffic uses VPN except applications marked Direct. With it disabled, only applications with a VPN rule use VPN.
The Direct rule uses the device’s normal connection and its system DNS settings, including Private DNS.
“Block” prevents traffic from the selected app only while VPN is running. App blocking in “Proxy” is available on Android 10 and later; web address blocking is available on Android 7 and later.

VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks/Outline, WireGuard, Hysteria2, Naive, TUIC and AnyTLS. Import connection links, HTTPS provider subscriptions including v2rayTun, compatible JSON, Clash/mihomo YAML, SIP008 JSON, dynamic Outline keys (ssconf://) and WireGuard. Supported server entries are imported from Clash/mihomo.
The package supports VLESS, Hysteria2, and WireGuard clients. Incoming connections use a separate Hysteria2 server module.
Profiles, exported configurations and subscription addresses may contain access secrets. Share them only with trusted people and routers. You can delete a VPN client profile at any time.
